utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, IT-98-33-A, the Prosecutor versus Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like now to have the appearances of the parties. First the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Appearing for the Prosecution is Norman Farrell. With me is Mr. Xavier Tracol, and our case manager is Ms. Lourdes Galicia. If I could just let you know that Mr. Tracol will be dealing with the Status Conference if there's any issues that arise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell. Now I would like appearances for the Defence. I understand that we will have a link by the telephone with Mr. Petrusic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Nenad Petrusic. You are entirely right; the Defence will speak for today's Status Conference via phone link.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Petrusic. General Krstic, can you hear the proceedings and understand me? THE APPELLANT: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The microphone is not on. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can hear and understand the proceedings. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: This is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires that the Status Conference be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody pending appeal the opportunity to raise issues in relations thereto, including the mental and physical condition of that person. The last appearance of General Krstic in court was at his appeal hearing, during 21 to 27 November 2003. General Krstic, I would like to ask you if you have any issues to raise in relation to your detention and specifically whether you have any concerns regarding your mental or physical well-being. General Krstic. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you very much for asking. I have no specific issues to raise, in terms of health problems, nor do I have any complaints about my -- the conditions of my detention at the Detention Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, General Krstic. You may be seated. As I have already noted, the last day of the appeal hearing in this case was on the 27th of November, 2003. The Appeals Chamber is still considering the appeal and hopes to issue the judgement in the course of this month. The other pending matter is the reasons for the Rule 115 decision delivered on the 5th of August and the 15th of September, 2003. The Appeals Chamber expects to deliver these reasons sometime within the next week. Does either of the parties wish to raise any other issue at this time? The Prosecution, do you have any issues that you would like to raise now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I hear that there are no issues that either the Prosecution or the Defence would like to raise with the Court today, so as there are no other issues, I thank the parties for their attendance and call the proceedings to a close.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
